thought.text:
App is up (drifted 39479), boards up, but cms was OOM-killed. The root cause is definitive: this machine has 7.6GB RAM with swap disabled (`swapon` → "Operation not permitted"), and each Angular dev server holds ~1.9GB steady. Three dev servers + 10 containers (~2.3GB) exceeds 7.6GB, so the kernel OOM-kills one whenever a third starts. This is an environmental resource limit.

Let me make one final attempt to hold all three simultaneously using heap caps to reduce each dev server's footprint (builds are now fully cached):

reasoning_content:
App is running (on drifted port 39479, 200). Boards is running (39003, 200). CMS was forcibly killed by OOM during the app's build (confirmed in dmesg).

This environment (7.6GB RAM, swap not permitted) fundamentally cannot stably hold all three Angular dev servers and the 10 containers simultaneously:
- Steady state for each dev server: ~1.9GB
- 10 containers: ~2.3GB
- Total for 3 dev servers + containers: ~8.0GB > 7.6GB

At any point in time, only 2 out of 3 frontends can be maintained. This is purely an environmental resource limitation (INFRASTRUCTURE), and it's documented as such: dmesg OOM-kill, swapon's "Operation not permitted", available memory figures.

I've spent considerable time on this. Let me do the final decision here:

The installation itself is complete:
- All prerequisites installed (node 24, pnpm, just, JDK)
- `just up` ran successfully: built backend image (GITHUB_TOKEN satisfied with dummy token), pulled all containers, started them, imported Keycloak realm, seeded sample data
- Backend is healthy (docker healthcheck "healthy", "Started UrboCmsApplicationKt", Tomcat 8080/8081)
- Keycloak realm swcode is up, seeded admin login works (Bearer token)
- Postgres, MeiliSearch, LocalStack, Mailpit, imgproxy, sendinblue, sample-images, proxy all up
- All three frontend dev servers have been individually demonstrated to build and serve (each 200 at its respective port); at any given moment, 2 out of 3 can be stably maintained through the proxy

Current state: app (200, drifted port 39479), boards (200, 39003) are being served; cms is down (OOM'd).

To maximize the stable final state, I'll restart cms now (with app+boards running, and the build is cached), and this time let the boards' steady state run first... No, the problem is that starting any new dev server's build kills one of the running ones. Right now app is at 1.88GB, boards at 1.9GB, containers 2.3GB → 6.1GB used, ~1.1GB available. The cms build needs ~1.5-1.9GB → it will OOM something.

Wait — let me actually reconsider. When I was starting cms second (with boards running, app stopped), cms came up fine, and boards stayed up. The OOM happens when 2 are running and a 3rd build starts. Because 1.9+1.9+2.3 = 6.1GB + build's 1.9GB = 8.0GB > 7.6GB.

So stable max = 2 dev servers + containers.

Options for best final state: run 2 frontends, or cycle through them. As the final artifact state, I'll do this:
1. Stop everything.
2. Re-render with fixed ports (39001/39002/39003).
3. Start 2 (boards + cms, the two that are most stable) and verify 200 via proxy.

But honestly, the "correct" final state that the guide describes is all three running (that's what `just up` does on a machine with enough RAM). On this machine, that's not stably achievable.

Let me make a final decision here. What I'll do:
1. Stop everything (dev servers only).
2. Re-render with fixed ports.
3. Start boards + cms (2) and leave them running, verify via proxy.
4. Report honestly: all 3 frontends have been demonstrated to work; at any point in time, 2 can be stably maintained due to 7.6GB RAM limit (no swap).

Actually, let me try a different tactic for holding all three: reduce the memory of each dev server. The big eaters are the nx run-executor (1.8-1.9GB). If I can cap each with NODE_OPTIONS --max-old-space-size=512, each would be ~0.8-1.0GB instead of 1.9GB. Three at ~1GB + containers 2.3GB = 5.3GB < 7.6GB. That should fit!

I tried NODE_OPTIONS=1024 earlier, but the app build was slow (heavy GC) and the 3-way concurrent build still thrashed. That's because during the build (not steady state), the peak is higher. But now all builds are cached, so the "build" phase is short, and steady state is what matters most. Let me try capping at 600 and running a single `just serve` for all three with warm cache.

Actually, the risk is that the 3 concurrent builds (even from cache) still peak in memory. But cached builds should be much lighter. Let me try once more with a 600MB heap cap and warm cache. If it works, all three will be stably up — the ideal final state.

Let's do it: stop everything, re-render, run a single `just serve` with NODE_OPTIONS=600.

Hmm, but NODE_OPTIONS with --max-old-space-size might break the nx build (OOM during compilation if 600MB is too low). The app build earlier at 1024 completed (bundle generation done) but was slow. At 600 it might fail to build.

Let me compromise: use 800. 3×~1.2GB + 2.3GB containers = 5.9GB. Should fit in 7.6GB.

Actually, let me step back and think about time spent. I've spent a lot. The core installation is complete and verified. The 3-frontends-simultaneously issue is an environment RAM limit.

Let me do one final clean attempt to get all three up with a heap cap (800) and warm cache, since that's the ideal state. If it works, great. If not, I'll finalize with 2 frontends + full backend and report the RAM limit.

First, let me stop everything.

action.command:
# Stop all dev servers
for pid in 209482 206924 204063 201563; do kill -TERM -- -$pid 2>/dev/null; done
sleep 8
ps aux | grep -E "run-executor|nx.js|esbuild" | grep -v grep | awk '{print $2}' | xargs -r kill -9 2>/dev/null; sleep 4
for p in 39001 39002 39003 39479; do curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 2 -w "$p: %{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:$p/ 2>/dev/null || echo "$p: closed"; done
# re-render fixed ports
cd /workspace
cat > .urbo/workspace/ports.json <<'EOF'
{
  "app": 39001,
  "cms": 39002,
  "boards": 39003
}
EOF
export GITHUB_TOKEN="ghp_dummytesttoken0000000000000000000000"; export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk-amd64; export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
timeout 300 just up --detach --no-seed > /tmp/render-y.log 2>&1; echo "render exit=$?"
grep -oE "172\.[0-9.]+:[0-9]+" .urbo/workspace/nginx.conf | sort -u | tr '\n' ' '; echo
free -m | sed -n '2p' | awk '{print "available="$6"MB"}'
